sections.h2: How do I reach the Portage County recorder in Ravenna?
sections.html:
The Portage County Recorder's office page prints a main line of (330) 297-3553, a fax at (330) 297-7349, and the same number for copy requests. Copy requests can also go by email to PCREC.COPIES@PORTAGECO.COM. Call before you drive a deed over to confirm counter hours.

Ravenna is the county seat, and the auditor's forms use 449 South Meridian Street as the county's address for property work. Whether you hand-carry a deed or mail it, start with the auditor on that street, because a conveyance has to be transferred there before the recorder will take it.

The office tells researchers that staff will not run searches for you. Staff will point you to the indexes and give help, and the page encourages anyone studying title or family history to use the recorder as a resource.

sections.h2: What does the Portage County recorder keep on file?
sections.html:
The recorder's description of the office says it keeps a permanent record of every document that conveys or burdens land in the county. Each filing is time stamped, given a document number, microfilmed and imaged, and indexed on the computer.

  • Deeds, mortgages and easements.
  • Land titles and rights-of-way.
  • Federal tax liens and unemployment liens.
  • Uniform Commercial Code filings.
  • Leases of several kinds, along with veteran discharges and records of veteran burials.

The office also collects the fees for what it records, sends the money to the county general fund and the state housing trust fund, and reminds commissioners and township trustees each year of their duty to file zoning resolutions and maps. For a seller, the practical point is that a mortgage release or lien release shows up in these same indexes, and the buyer's title company will look for them before closing.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Portage County?
sections.html:
The county's fee page says the state of Ohio's recording fees apply and adds one warning: a document that does not follow the state's marginal rule is charged an extra $20.00 on top of the recording fees. The dollar figures below come from the statute, R.C. 317.32.

  • First two pages: a $17 base fee plus a $17 housing trust fund fee.
  • Each page after that: $4 base plus $4 housing trust fund.
  • A document preservation surcharge of up to $5, credited to the county general fund.
  • Certifying a copy: $1 base plus $1 trust fund per page.
  • Each marginal reference in a separate instrument: $2 base plus $2 trust fund.

A county can set the surcharge anywhere up to the cap, so ask the recorder for the total on your exact document. Pages are counted at 8.5 by 14 inches or fraction of a page, caption page included.

sections.h2: What does the Portage County auditor charge before a deed goes to the recorder?
sections.html:
The auditor's side comes first. The county auditor's transfer page says the real estate department transfers deeds and other transfer documents before they are recorded, and it publishes a conveyance fee of $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price, plus 50 cents for each parcel being transferred. The DTE 100 form, Conveyance of Real Property, goes with the deed.

Use the rate Portage County prints, not a figure quoted for another county. Ohio law also lets a county board adopt a real property transfer tax of up to 30 cents per hundred dollars of value, paid by the grantor to the auditor before the deed is presented to the recorder (R.C. 322.02). Ask the auditor whether this county has one in force.

The same auditor's pages also offer parcel ownership histories, valuations, sales information and tax data, which are worth printing before you meet a buyer.

sections.h2: Which Portage County offices does a seller contact?
sections.html:
Three desks handle most of a sale, and each prints something different for the public.

Portage County offices a home seller usually needs, with what each published
OfficeTask in a saleWhat it publishes
RecorderRecords the deed, mortgage and releasesMain (330) 297-3553; fax (330) 297-7349; online index called Find My Deed
AuditorTransfers the deed, sets the conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 plus 50 cents per parcel; DTE 100 form
TreasurerBills and collects property taxTwo bills a year, about half in February and half in July

The treasurer's schedule matters because the deed does not settle unpaid tax. Ask the treasurer for a payoff on the parcel, and ask the title company how the current half will be divided between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: Can I search Portage County land records myself?
sections.html:
Yes. The recorder's page links a "Find My Deed" search, and the county posts scanned lease books on its site, with books numbered 92 through 114 posted so far and more promised as scanning continues. The office warns that its indexes default to one page for some older volumes and pages, so documents shown as a single page may run longer. Call or email the office for correct page totals before you order copies.

Copies of all records are available on request. Because the recorder staff will not search for you, bring a parcel number or the names on the deed. The auditor's property search gives the owner history and sales for a parcel, which narrows what to ask for.

The state's rule on documents also applies here: Ohio requires a conveyance to be prepared and signed under the Revised Code before it is accepted for record. The recorder's page says so in plain terms.

sections.h2: What else should a Portage County seller know about recording?
sections.html:
Portage County is 504 square miles of Northeast Ohio, and the county's about page says the General Assembly created it in 1808. Wikipedia reports a 2020 population of 161,791 and says 31.1% of occupied homes are rented.

  • Format the deed to Ohio's page and margin rules to avoid the $20 surcharge.
  • Record a mortgage satisfaction soon after payoff, so the buyer's title search is clean.
  • Take the deed to the auditor for transfer before it goes to the recorder.

If you are working out a sale of a house with liens, back taxes or a stalled estate, a direct cash purchase avoids most of this paperwork on your side. The buyer's closing agent handles the filings.

faqs.q: What is the Portage County recorder's phone number?
faqs.a: The main line is (330) 297-3553, and the fax is (330) 297-7349. Copy requests use the same phone number and also go by email to PCREC.COPIES@PORTAGECO.COM.

faqs.q: How much does the Portage County auditor charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The auditor's page lists $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel. That is separate from the recorder's fee, and the auditor processes the transfer first.

faqs.q: Is there an extra recording fee in Portage County?
faqs.a: Yes, in one case. A document that does not follow Ohio's marginal rule is charged an extra $20.00 on top of the normal recording fees, so check margins and fonts before you submit.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Portage County deed online?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder's page links a Find My Deed search, and the auditor's real estate site shows ownership history and sales. The recorder warns that page counts on older volumes can be wrong, so confirm them by phone.

faqs.q: Does the recorder pay off my mortgage or my taxes?
faqs.a: No. The recorder only records the documents. Payoffs go through your lender and the county treasurer, and a title or closing agent normally handles both at the closing table.
